main_text.p: nem urget. 4. quia utilitatem aliquam simul affert, quòd um- bratilis quædam inde nascatur conjugationum, temporum, modorum, personarum, numero- rum, &c. cognitio, quæ paulò post faciliorem memoriæ labo- rem conciliat. Continuetur per dies circiter quindecim.

Secundum exercitium Lec- tionis sit in Textu Biblico. Ra- tio, quia cùm singulæ voces hîc sint aliæ & novæ, ideoque lectio nonnihil tardior & operosior, ad eam non est accedendum, nisi linguâ & pronunciatione in fací- lioribus, nonnihil prius assuefa- ctâ & informatâ. Continuetur per dies quindecim alios.
Tota hæc exercitatio fiat præ- sente præceptore, aut aliquo do- ctiore, qui linguam errantem di- rigat, & pronunciationem pra- vam

page.notes: Page has a dark blotch at the lower left and a stain at the left edge; the ink of the last line is partly obscured. The word "Lectionis" and "Ratio" are set with a hyphen split at the line end (Lec-tionis, Ra-tio). The final word "vam" is the catchword, not part of the text; it may be read as "pravam" split across lines, so I have kept "vam" in the text as the last line word. No page number, running head or signature is printed.
